lastText: OHLLAGEBERICHTHome19141915191619171918-2MANPOWER-4MUNITIONS-1HOME FRONTXI.1918The RequestThe army in the west is not broken in the sense the word is used in staff colleges. It is retreating in order, on ground it still holds, in front of an enemy it can still hurt. What has gone is the possibility of any outcome except a worse one later. The submarine campaign did what its critics said it would do and did not do what its authors promised. The Americans are here in numbers, and the six months in the memorandum expired a long time ago. The request goes forward from the Supreme Command. It is a military judgment, made by soldiers, and within a few years a great many people who were in this building will say it was made by someone else.Settled recordChief of the General Staff at the close: Hindenburg. The war ends on the eleventh of November. Lorraine, August 1914: conceded, as the plan required. The Marne: delegated forward under plenipotentiary authority. The Meuse: fought as the directive was written. The submarines: unrestricted from 1 February 1917. Weight of effort after the Marne: held in the west. Posture for 1917: defensive, rebuilding. American entry: brought on by the decision of 9 January 1917. Brest-Litovsk: narrow settlement, divisions released west. Spring 1918: Amiens named as the objective. September 1918: requested through a new civil government.Return to file
